Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

remind verb

make someone remember

also remind someone of, remind someone to, reminder, thanks for reminding me

classical

Cic. Top. 5: admonitus hujus aeris aliēnī (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 35.13: admonēre aliquem foederis (Lewis & Short)

admoneō, admonēre, admonuī, admonitum

verb, second conjugation; the person in the accusative, the thing in the genitive or with dē, an action with ut or nē

remind (someone of something; to do something)

To put someone in mind of a thing, kindly (Lewis & Short); also to advise and to warn. The simple moneō serves too, especially in thanks: bene monēs.

Other words

  • commonefaciō, commonefacere, commonefēcī, commonefactum — remind forcibly, impress upon

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.72.1: etiam atque etiam esse commonefaciendum (Lewis & Short)

    Stronger than admonēre: to remind again and again (Lewis & Short: “most freq. in Cic.”). So too commoneō.

Examples

  • admonitus hujus aeris aliēnī

    reminded of this debtCic. Top. 5 (Lewis & Short)

  • sōl mē invītābat, famēs admonēbat, nūbēs minābantur

    the sun invited me out, hunger reminded me, the clouds threatenedSen. Ep. 46.1

  • Bene monēs, paene istud oblītus eram.

    Thanks for reminding me, I had nearly forgotten.Cord. Coll. 1.2 (not classical)

See also remember, forget, memory.
